- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is mixed or neutral; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecasts >+10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For long-term (last 10+ days) forecasts, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth with 3-day moving average of true values if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
